issues.failure_explanation: The derivation of the Lipschitz bound in (7.16) for the quasilinear model assumes the existence of a constant $C_\infty > 0$ such that $\|v\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} \le C_\infty \|v\|_V$ for all $v \in V$. Since $V = H_0^1(\Omega)$ on polyhedral domains $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $d \in \{2,3\}$, $H_0^1(\Omega)$ does not continuously embed into $L^\infty(\Omega)$, so no such constant $C_\infty$ exists. Furthermore, quasilinear elliptic operators of the form $-\nabla \cdot (a(u)\nabla u)$ are not Fréchet differentiable from $H_0^1(\Omega)$ to $H^{-1}(\Omega)$ in dimensions $d \ge 2$, meaning condition (C3) cannot be certified in this setting.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must restrict the model to dimension $d=1$ or reformulate the verification framework in a stronger function space (such as $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ with $p > d$) where the quasilinear operator is Fréchet differentiable and embeds into $L^\infty(\Omega)$.
issues.overall_effect: The Lipschitz bound (7.16) and the claim that the quasilinear diffusion model satisfies condition (C3) fail in dimensions $d \in \{2,3\}$. The quasilinear problem class cannot be certified within the $H_0^1(\Omega)$ functional framework.
issues.title: Invalid L-infinity embedding assumption for quasilinear diffusion in H1_0
issues.why_classification: Because $H_0^1(\Omega) \not\hookrightarrow L^\infty(\Omega)$ for $d \in \{2,3\}$ and the quasilinear operator is not Fréchet differentiable on $H_0^1(\Omega)$, resolving the defect requires either excluding the multidimensional regime or adopting a different functional and proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose Algorithm~\ref{alg:rho} enters the bisection phase with a bracket $0<\rho_{\rm low}<\rho_{\rm up}$ such that $\mathsf{Adm}(\rho_{\rm low})$ is true and $\mathsf{Adm}(\rho_{\rm up})$ is false.

issues.failure_explanation: In Algorithm 1, if the initial trial radius $\rho = 2\eta$ fails, lines 6--14 attempt to find an admissible radius by repeatedly halving $\rho_{\rm up} = 2\eta$. However, for any $\rho \le \eta$, $p(\rho) = (\eta - \rho) + \frac{L(\rho)}{2\alpha}\rho^2 > 0$ strictly because $\eta - \rho \ge 0$ and $\frac{L(\rho)}{2\alpha}\rho^2 > 0$. Every candidate generated in the loop has $\rho_{\rm low} = 2\eta / 2^j \le \eta$ for $j \ge 1$, so $p(\rho_{\rm low}) > 0$ holds identically. As a result, the condition at line 9 is never met, the loop never breaks, line 16 always returns fail, and the bisection phase (lines 18--27) is mathematically unreachable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the halving loop with a search on $(\eta, 2\eta)$ (e.g., evaluating $p$ at its minimum or via bisection on $[\eta, 2\eta]$) when $2\eta \ge \rho_+$, or an expanding search when $2\eta < \rho_-$, and update the proof of Proposition A.3 accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 1 always fails whenever the initial guess $2\eta$ is inadmissible, even when the admissible set $\mathcal{AD} = [\rho_-, \rho_+)$ is non-empty. Proposition A.3 rests on an impossible hypothesis ('enters the bisection phase') and is unproven.
issues.title: Shrinking search in verification radius selection cannot find an admissible radius
issues.why_classification: The failure is confined to the scalar one-dimensional search strategy in Algorithm 1. It can be fully resolved with a contained algorithmic redesign of the bracketing step without disrupting the broader certification workflow.
